newsitem.title: UK: Heavy demand boosts July cash Brent, N.Sea grades.
newsitem.headline: Heavy demand boosts July cash Brent, N.Sea grades.

text.p: Heavy demand for fast disappearing July North Sea cargoes pushed the front-month spread on the cash Brent market into backwardation on Tuesday, brokers said.
July/August firmed on overnight chat in the U.S. and was talked at +0.03/+0.10 in Europe, though nothing was seen changing hands.

Following months were still in contango, though flatter, with August/September trading at -4 cents. Sept/October moved at -4 and -5 cents. A Wall Street trading house was the buyer in all three cases.
"It's firming across the board," said one trader. But with Iraqi barrels predicted to hit the market in August he doubted the entire complex would slip into backwardation.
The market consensus was that Iraqi crude was unlikely to flow until August, in line with comments made by Iraqi envoy Abdul Amir al-Anbari in recent days.

Rising prices for physical barrels have hit refinery margins hard in Europe and the Mediterranean and traders said it appeared likely simpler processing plants would soon have to cut runs, taking the steam out of demand.

"I see worsening margins and increasing premia and I'm wondering how long that will last," said a trader. Outright values were also up on fund buying, with IPE August Brent futures 13 cents better on $18.64 at 1200 GMT.
No physical North Sea cargoes were seen traded on Tuesday morning, partly because last week's rush of buying had cleared out most of July availability.
Only three Forties cargoes were reckoned still on offer, and one large Scandinavian seller had just eight cargoes left from the 45 or so on his programme for July.
"That's incredibly low for this time of the month," the seller said. Less than 10 Ekofisk were thought available.
One Brent cargo was due to be nominated from the paper chains on Tuesday.

"The paper market is going to assume the ascendancy in the short-term," one trader said. "I can foresee buyers starting to request confidentiality soon because the numbers on the physical will just be so outrageous."
Short-term swaps firmed as spreads narrowed. Contracts for differences for next week were bid at 16 cents below August but not heard offered.
Mediterranean sour crude markets held firm with regional benchmark Russian Urals valued around Dated Brent -65/-60 cents.

Most first half July cargoes were seen committed, but traders said refiners may release barrels to take advantage of current high prices. Only buyers with very prompt needs were expected to venture into the market.
"If you have to cover prompt then you have to buy, but if you can possibly wait for (Iraqi) Kirkuk then you will," said one trader.
Traders said that negative Urals hydroskimming margins would keep a lid on differentials.
While a wider Brent-Dubai spread has stifled sales of West African crude to the Far East, traders said July-loading barrels were more or less sold.
"It's quiet but it's balanced," said one dealer.
Bonny Light was pegged at Dated Brent +45/47, steady on recent traded levels.
-- S. Maguire, R.Russell, London newsroom =44 171 542 8060
